sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, basically…
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上……

sentences.en: Their currency has been inflated to pay for the war.
sentences.zh: 他们的货币为了支付战争费用而通货膨胀了。

sentences.en: So, incredible figure that taxation only covered 14% of German government expenditure through the war.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个令人难以置信的数据是，税收仅覆盖了德国政府战争期间支出的14%。

sentences.en: I mean, incredibly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难以置信。

sentences.en: That's incredible.
sentences.zh: 那太不可思议了。

sentences.en: So, the rest…
sentences.zh: 所以，剩下的……

sentences.en: That is incredible.
sentences.zh: 那真是不可思议。

sentences.en: It's debt and inflation, exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是债务和通货膨胀。

sentences.en: So, they're kind of pauperizing themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们某种程度上是在让自己变得贫困。

sentences.en: And that obviously will be very important in the post-war years.
sentences.zh: 这显然在战后几年会非常重要。

sentences.en: Democracy has not exactly been suspended, but it's been sort of pushed to the margins because by the end of the war, the country is being run by a duumvirate of two generals,
sentences.zh: 民主并没有完全被暂停，但它被推到了边缘，因为到战争结束时，这个国家由两位将军组成的二头政治统治，

sentences.en: General Hindenburg, Paul von Hindenburg, and General Eric Ludendorff, who we will definitely be talking about later on.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡将军，保罗·冯·兴登堡，以及埃里希·鲁登道夫将军，我们稍后肯定会谈到他。

sentences.en: So, this is to keep it together.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是为了保持团结。

sentences.en: This is to kind of keep fighting.
sentences.zh: 这是为了继续战斗。

sentences.en: And then, partly because of press censorship and so on, the German people are astonished when it all falls apart in November 1918.
sentences.zh: 然后，部分由于新闻审查制度等原因，当1918年11月一切崩溃时，德国人民感到震惊。

sentences.en: And almost without anybody really knowing what's going on, the Kaiser is suddenly out.
sentences.zh: 几乎在没人真正知道发生了什么的情况下，德皇突然下台了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's out kind of overnight.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他几乎一夜之间就下台了。

sentences.en: And a republic has been proclaimed in Berlin by people, many of whom did not even want a republic.
sentences.zh: 柏林宣布成立了共和国，而宣布的人中，许多人甚至根本不想要共和国。

sentences.en: So, most famously Friedrich Ebert, who's the leader of the Social Democrats.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是弗里德里希·艾伯特，他是社会民主党的领袖。

sentences.en: He proclaims the republic, even though he actually wanted to keep the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 他宣布了共和国，尽管他实际上想保留君主制。

sentences.en: So, the whole thing is falling apart in chaos.
sentences.zh: 所以，整个事情都在混乱中分崩离析。

sentences.en: Berlin is wracked in the winter of 1918-19 by fighting between different left-wing factions.
sentences.zh: 1918-19年的冬天，柏林饱受不同左翼派系之间战斗的蹂躏。

sentences.en: There's rebellions.
sentences.zh: 发生了叛乱。

sentences.en: There's an uprising by a group of people called the Spartacists on the left that is put down by returning soldiers from the war.
sentences.zh: 左翼一个名为斯巴达克同盟的团体发动了起义，被从战争中返回的士兵镇压了。

sentences.en: So, total and utter chaos.
sentences.zh: 所以，完全彻底的混乱。

sentences.en: Everything has suddenly collapsed in ruins.
sentences.zh: 一切突然坍塌成废墟。

sentences.en: And ordinary Germans, particularly those who fought in the war, are completely horrified and taken unawares by this.
sentences.zh: 普通的德国人，特别是那些参加过战争的人，对此感到完全震惊和措手不及。

sentences.en: And there's a very, very famous example, which I'll just read to you before we go into the break.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常、非常著名的例子，在进入休息之前，我读给你听。

sentences.en: So, it's a guy who's a corporal.
sentences.zh: 这是一个下士。

sentences.en: He's been a corporal.
sentences.zh: 他一直是一名下士。

sentences.en: He's won the Iron Cross.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了铁十字勋章。

sentences.en: He's well regarded by his comrades for his bravery.
sentences.zh: 他因勇敢而受到战友们的尊敬。

sentences.en: He's not yet 30.
sentences.zh: 他还没到30岁。

sentences.en: And he had been blinded in a gas attack near Ypres in the final weeks of the war.
sentences.zh: 他在战争最后几周伊普尔附近的一次毒气袭击中失明了。

sentences.en: And he's ended up in a hospital in a place called Passavalk in Pomerania.
sentences.zh: 他最终住进了波美拉尼亚帕塞瓦尔克的一家医院。

sentences.en: And in the hospital, he's been hearing rumors of what's all going wrong.
sentences.zh: 在医院里，他一直听到关于局势恶化的传言。

sentences.en: And then on the 10th of November, so literally the day before the war ends, a Protestant pastor comes to visit the hospital to give a speech to them.
sentences.zh: 然后在11月10日，也就是战争结束的前一天，一位新教牧师来到医院向他们发表演讲。

sentences.en: And he later told the story.
sentences.zh: 他后来讲述了这段经历。

sentences.en: He said, I was in a fever of excitement as I listened to the address.
sentences.zh: 他说，当他听着那番演讲时，内心感到一阵狂热的激动。

sentences.en: The reverend old gentleman seemed to be trembling when he informed us that the House of Hohenzollern should no longer wear the imperial crown.
sentences.zh: 那位年迈的牧师在告诉我们霍亨索伦家族将不再佩戴帝国皇冠时，似乎在颤抖。

sentences.en: The Fatherland had become a republic, that we should pray to the Almighty not to withhold his blessing, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 祖国已经变成了一个共和国，我们应该祈求全能的主不要收回他的祝福，等等，等等，等等，等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: And then the pastor breaks down and he starts crying.
sentences.zh: 然后牧师崩溃了，开始哭泣。

sentences.en: And the soldier says, the corporal says,
sentences.zh: 士兵说，那个下士说，

sentences.en: A feeling of profound dismay fell on the people in that assembly.
sentences.zh: 一种深深的沮丧感笼罩了在场的人。

sentences.en: And I do not think there was a single eye that withheld its tears.
sentences.zh: 我想当时没有一个人能忍住泪水。

sentences.en: As for myself,
sentences.zh: 至于我自己，

sentences.en: I broke down completely when the old gentleman tried to resume his story by informing us that we must now end this long war because the war was lost and we're at the mercy of the victor.
sentences.zh: 当那位老先生试图继续讲下去，告诉我们必须结束这场漫长的战争，因为战争已经失败，我们只能任由胜利者摆布时，我彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: It was impossible for me to stay and listen any longer.
sentences.zh: 我无法再待下去听他讲了。

sentences.en: Darkness surrounded me as I staggered and stumbled back to my ward and I buried my aching head between the blankets and the pillow.
sentences.zh: 黑暗笼罩着我，我踉踉跄跄地回到病房，把疼痛的头埋在毯子和枕头之间。

sentences.en: I had not cried since the day I stood beside my mother's grave.
sentences.zh: 自从站在母亲墓前的那天起，我就再也没有哭过。

sentences.en: And Dominic, the name of that corporal, what was it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那个下士的名字，到底叫什么？

sentences.en: It was, of course, Tom, Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 当然是汤姆，阿道夫·希特勒。

sentences.en: See you after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后见。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: We are looking at the rise to power of the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 我们正在探讨纳粹的崛起。

sentences.en: And Dominic, just before the break, you introduced Adolf Hitler having a, well, basically losing it over Germany having been defeated.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，就在休息之前，你介绍了阿道夫·希特勒，嗯，基本上是因为德国战败而情绪失控。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Breaking down and sobbing like a baby beside his mother's grave.
sentences.zh: 在母亲墓前像个孩子一样崩溃痛哭。

sentences.en: So we did an episode, we did two episodes on Hitler, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们做过一期节目，我们做了两期关于希特勒的节目，不是吗？

sentences.en: On the life of Hitler with Sir Ian Kershaw.
sentences.zh: 关于伊恩·克肖爵士笔下的希特勒生平。

sentences.en: But just give us a brief reminder for those who didn't listen to that and who may not know about Hitler's background.
sentences.zh: 但请为那些没听过那期节目、可能不了解希特勒背景的人简单回顾一下。

sentences.en: Where does he come from?
sentences.zh: 他来自哪里？

sentences.en: Sir Hitler is Austrian.
sentences.zh: 希特勒是奥地利人。

sentences.en: And I think, as Sir Ian would undoubtedly say, the salient thing about Hitler is that up to this point, he is a nobody.
sentences.zh: 我想，正如伊恩爵士无疑会说的那样，关于希特勒最显著的一点是，直到这一刻，他还是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: There is nothing remarkable about him at all.
sentences.zh: 他身上没有任何特别之处。

sentences.en: He's not particularly, he doesn't appear particularly evil.
sentences.zh: 他并不特别，看起来也不怎么邪恶。

sentences.en: He's a bit of a failure.
sentences.zh: 他有点失败。

sentences.en: He's just a bit of a dropout.
sentences.zh: 他只是个有点辍学倾向的人。

sentences.en: So he was born in a place in Austria called Braunau am Inn on Easter Saturday, 1889.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1889年的复活节星期六，在奥地利一个叫布劳瑙的地方。

sentences.en: He's the fourth child of his Alois and Clara.
sentences.zh: 他是阿洛伊斯和克拉拉的第四个孩子。

sentences.en: So Alois, his father, is just a sort of slightly rubbishy kind of bad-tempered Austrian customs official.
sentences.zh: 阿洛伊斯，也就是他的父亲，只是一个有点糟糕、脾气暴躁的奥地利海关官员。

sentences.en: He's a civil servant, a sort of minor civil servant.
sentences.zh: 他是一名公务员，算是一种低级公务员。

sentences.en: So no Jewish ancestry?
sentences.zh: 所以没有犹太血统？

sentences.en: No, no, nothing.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有，什么都没有。

sentences.en: So Ian dealt with that myth.
sentences.zh: 伊恩已经处理过那个传言了。

sentences.en: And he also dealt with the myth that Hitler only had one ball.
sentences.zh: 他还处理了关于希特勒只有一个睾丸的传言。

sentences.en: Tom, you love that.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你很喜欢这个。

sentences.en: You love that detail, which is completely untrue.
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢这个细节，但这完全是不真实的。

sentences.en: Those are the questions that the listeners will be asking.
sentences.zh: 这些都是听众会问的问题。

sentences.en: And we just want to, you know, put that down.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想，你知道，澄清一下。

sentences.en: So the idea that there's some sort of physical or extraordinary psychological flaw is not right.
sentences.zh: 所以，认为他有什么生理或非凡心理缺陷的想法是不对的。

sentences.en: It's a cop out.
sentences.zh: 这是一种逃避。

sentences.en: What we know about Hitler when he was a little boy is that he's perfectly normal and a happy boy.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的希特勒小时候的情况是，他是一个非常正常且快乐的男孩。

sentences.en: I mean, Ian Kershaw in his biography describes him playing with his friends in the woods and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我是说，伊恩·克肖在传记中描述他和小伙伴在树林里玩耍等等。

sentences.en: In 1900, when he's about 11, he moves to a bigger school in the city of Linz.
sentences.zh: 1900年，他大约11岁时，搬到了林茨市的一所更大的学校。

sentences.en: And there, I mean, again, this is really not that exceptional.
sentences.zh: 在那里，我的意思是，这真的没什么特别的。

sentences.en: He's at a big school now, bigger place, doesn't really know anybody, is very miserable, kind of is lazy, becomes a bit of a dropout, becomes a sort of sullen surly.
sentences.zh: 他现在在一所大学校，更大的地方，谁也不认识，非常痛苦，有点懒惰，变得有点辍学，变得阴沉暴躁。

sentences.en: Oh, leave me alone.
sentences.zh: 哦，别管我。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He tells his father famously, you know, I want to go and be an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 他很有名地告诉他父亲，你知道，我想去当个艺术家。

sentences.en: And his father shouts at him and says, never.
sentences.zh: 他父亲对他大喊大叫，说，绝不。

sentences.en: Just hanging out in his room.
sentences.zh: 只是待在他的房间里。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: His father drops dead in 1903.
sentences.zh: 他父亲在1903年突然去世了。

sentences.en: Adolf, who's his, you know, the apple of his mother's eye, is able to persuade her that he could let him drop out of school.
sentences.zh: 阿道夫，也就是他母亲的掌上明珠，能够说服她让他辍学。

sentences.en: Then he just spends his time daydreaming and going to concerts.
sentences.zh: 然后他就把时间花在做白日梦和去听音乐会上。

sentences.en: But also, because that's the thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这也是重点，不是吗？

sentences.en: The stereotype of the teenager in his room listening to music.
sentences.zh: 青少年待在房间里听音乐的刻板印象。

sentences.en: I mean, Hitler becomes obsessed by Wagner.
sentences.zh: 我是说，希特勒变得痴迷于瓦格纳。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, really, completely obsessed by Wagner.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的，完全痴迷于瓦格纳。

sentences.en: And you can completely see why this sullen, rather miserable teenager is obsessed by a composer who celebrates the hero.
sentences.zh: 你可以完全理解为什么这个阴沉、相当痛苦的青少年会痴迷于一位歌颂英雄的作曲家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who conquers, you know, stands atop the blooded bodies of his enemies.
sentences.zh: 谁征服了，你知道，站在敌人的血肉之躯上。

sentences.en: And there are so many, again and again in his operas, the figure of the hero is someone who hasn't been recognized as a hero, who kind of emerges from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 在他的歌剧中，英雄的形象一次又一次地出现，是一个没有被承认为英雄的人，从虚无中崛起。

sentences.en: So you can absolutely see that, A, this makes Hitler, you know, you can see the kind of person he is.
sentences.zh: 所以你绝对可以理解，首先，这让希特勒，你知道，你可以看出他是哪种人。

sentences.en: But you also can, I think most listeners would say, this is not a particularly unusual person.
sentences.zh: 但我想大多数听众也会说，这并不是一个特别不寻常的人。

sentences.en: I mean, there's one in, there are multiple versions of this person in schools, the length and breadth of England, and they will go on to become loss adjusters, estate agents,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在英国的学校里，这种人有多个版本，他们以后会成为理赔员、房地产经纪人，

sentences.en: small business advisors, you know, perfectly normal people.
sentences.zh: 小企业顾问，你知道，完全正常的人。

sentences.en: So what happens to set Hitler on the path that makes him Hitler?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么让希特勒走上了成为希特勒的道路呢？

sentences.en: I suppose, so one crucial thing is him going to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 我想，关键的一点是他去了维也纳。

sentences.en: So his mother dies in 1907 when he's 18.
sentences.zh: 他母亲在1907年去世时，他18岁。

sentences.en: He's tried to get into the Fine Arts Academy in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他曾试图进入维也纳美术学院。

sentences.en: He doesn't get in twice.
sentences.zh: 他两次都没考上。

sentences.en: Very disappointed by that.
sentences.zh: 对此非常失望。

sentences.en: It's a crushing blow to him because he's dreamed of being an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 这对他是沉重的打击，因为他梦想成为一名艺术家。

sentences.en: He ends up as a kind of dropout in a men's hostel, the men's home, and he's painting pictures for tourists, so postcards famously.
sentences.zh: 他最终成了一个住在男子旅舍的辍学者，男子之家，他为游客画画，也就是著名的明信片。

sentences.en: He gets certain things from Vienna that he perhaps wouldn't have got somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 他在维也纳得到了一些他在别处可能得不到的东西。

sentences.en: So Vienna is, of course, in Austria, it's a largely German-speaking city, but it is the capital of the Habsburg Empire, what we commonly call Austria.
sentences.zh: 维也纳当然是在奥地利，它是一个主要讲德语的城市，但它是哈布斯堡帝国的首都，也就是我们通常所说的奥地利。

sentences.en: He's spending all his time listening to Wagner.
sentences.zh: 他把所有时间都花在听瓦格纳上。

sentences.en: Wagner's very popular in Vienna, but he's also reading stuff.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳在维也纳很受欢迎，但他也在读一些东西。

sentences.en: There's a kind of strain of antisemitism that's particularly pronounced in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 维也纳有一种特别明显的反犹太主义倾向。

sentences.en: It's particularly virulent because Vienna is a city that is torn apart, really, by kind of political and racial conflicts.
sentences.zh: 它特别恶毒，因为维也纳是一个被政治和种族冲突撕裂的城市。

sentences.en: The Habsburg Empire is multi-ethnic.
sentences.zh: 哈布斯堡帝国是多民族的。

sentences.en: Right, because in Germany, there isn't much mainstream political antisemitism.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为在德国，没有多少主流的政治反犹太主义。

sentences.en: It's on the edges.
sentences.zh: 它只在边缘地带。

sentences.en: But in Vienna, that's different.
sentences.zh: 但在维也纳，情况不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So Kershaw says in his biography, you know, when Hitler goes down to the newspaper kiosk outside the men's home or wherever, it's full of racist periodicals.
sentences.zh: 所以克肖在传记中说，你知道，当希特勒走到男子之家外面的报刊亭时，那里到处都是种族主义期刊。

sentences.en: So we know that he read something called Ostara.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道他读过一种叫《奥斯塔拉》的东西。

sentences.en: We think he read something called Ostara by a guy called Jörg Lanz, which was all about kind of menacing, dark, swarthy figures attacking blonde women, and it's very,
sentences.zh: 我们认为他读过一个叫约尔格·兰茨的人写的《奥斯塔拉》，内容全是关于威胁性的、黑暗的、皮肤黝黑的人物攻击金发女性，而且非常，

sentences.en: very antisemitic.
sentences.zh: 非常反犹太。

sentences.en: But the key figure, I know you're very interested in, Tom, is this guy Georg Ritter von Schoenere.
sentences.zh: 但关键人物，我知道你很感兴趣，汤姆，是这个叫格奥尔格·里特·冯·舍内雷的人。
zh_words: 格奥尔格·里特·冯·舍内雷

sentences.en: Yes, he wanted to get rid of the Christian calendar, and he hated Christianity.
sentences.zh: 是的，他想废除基督教历法，他讨厌基督教。

sentences.en: He wanted to give all the Christian festivals German names.
sentences.zh: 他想给所有的基督教节日起德语名字。

sentences.en: So, you know, Christmas wanted to be Euler Fest and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，圣诞节想叫尤勒节等等。

sentences.en: But he also wants to get rid of the Christian dating system and replace it with the date of a defeat of the Romans by the Cimbri and the Teutons.
sentences.zh: 但他还想废除基督教纪年系统，用辛布里人和条顿人击败罗马人的日期来代替。

sentences.en: So that's just before Marius, at the Battle of Nerea, and that this should be the equivalent of Grand Zero, the birth of Jesus, replace the birth of Jesus, Battle of Nerea.
sentences.zh: 那是在马略之前，在内雷亚战役，这应该相当于零点，耶稣的诞生，取代耶稣的诞生，内雷亚战役。

sentences.en: That's what it's all about, which is such a kind of eccentric, mad thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的全部意义，这是一种非常古怪、疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: It's expressive of the kind of the strain of lunatic thinking that characterizes antisemitism.
sentences.zh: 它表达了那种构成反犹太主义特征的疯狂思想。

sentences.en: Yeah, but Schoenere is important.
sentences.zh: 是的，但舍内雷很重要。

sentences.en: So Schoenere is, he's a sort of quite a popular thinker in Vienna at the time,
sentences.zh: 所以舍内雷是，他是当时维也纳一位相当受欢迎的思想家，

sentences.en: because he's proposing also things like universal manhood suffrage and kind of greater state activism and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为他还提出了诸如普选权和更大的国家行动主义等建议。

sentences.en: So he's hard to pin down politically.
sentences.zh: 所以他在政治上很难被定义。

sentences.en: But some of his ideas are definitely going to be very influential.
sentences.zh: 但他的一些想法肯定会产生很大的影响。

sentences.en: Schoenere, for example, wants to push the antisemitism further than anybody else.
sentences.zh: 例如，舍内雷想把反犹太主义推得比任何人都远。

sentences.en: He wants to remove Jews completely from the life of, yeah, so physically, politically.
sentences.zh: 他想把犹太人完全从生活中移除，是的，在身体上，在政治上。

sentences.en: And he's also the guy who comes up with the Heil, right?
sentences.zh: 而且他也是那个提出“希特勒万岁”（Heil）的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And his followers call him Fuhrer, leader.
sentences.zh: 他的追随者称他为“元首”（Fuhrer）。

sentences.en: So the old Roman stuff that you were just mentioning, he starts shouting Heil when he's in parliament in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才提到的那些古罗马的东西，他在20世纪初在议会时开始高喊“万岁”。

sentences.en: And his followers, yeah, they call him the leader.
sentences.zh: 而他的追随者，是的，他们称他为领袖。

sentences.en: So this sort of Cod Roman, you know, that the Nazis are going to pick up on that later on.
sentences.zh: 所以这种伪罗马的东西，你知道，纳粹后来会沿用这一点。

sentences.en: There's also another key character in Vienna, very important influence upon Hitler and Nazism, is the mayor of Vienna.
sentences.zh: 维也纳还有另一个关键人物，对希特勒和纳粹主义有非常重要的影响，那就是维也纳市长。

sentences.en: He's called Karl Luger.
sentences.zh: 他叫卡尔·卢格。

sentences.en: Again, very hard to pin down politically because he's like a sort of anti-Semitic Viennese Joseph Chamberlain, the great mayor of Birmingham, Victorian Britain,
sentences.zh: 同样，在政治上很难定义，因为他就像一个反犹太的维也纳版约瑟夫·张伯伦，维多利亚时代英国伯明翰的伟大市长，

sentences.en: because he carries out all these great municipal reforMs.
sentences.zh: 因为他进行了所有这些伟大的市政改革。

sentences.en: So he really modernizes Vienna and he does stuff for the working classes and the low middle classes and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实使维也纳现代化了，他为工人阶级和中下层阶级做了很多事情等等。

sentences.en: But he wins support by being fanatically and virulently anti-Semitic.
sentences.zh: 但他通过狂热和恶毒的反犹太主义赢得了支持。

sentences.en: And we know.
sentences.zh: 我们知道。

sentences.en: So he's a national socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个民族社会主义者。

sentences.en: He's a nationalist socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一个民族社会主义者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We know that Hitler said to people in his men's hostel, oh, Luger is a brilliant man, he's the best mayor of any German in history.
sentences.zh: 我们知道希特勒在男子旅舍对人们说，哦，卢格是个天才，他是历史上任何德国人中最好的市长。

sentences.en: So again, he's picking up all of this stuff and he's probably picking up, he's almost certainly picking up the anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，他正在吸收所有这些东西，他很可能正在吸收，几乎可以肯定是在吸收反犹太主义。

sentences.en: So there's some debate about exactly when Hitler becomes anti-Semitic, but he cannot not have been influenced by it.
sentences.zh: 所以关于希特勒到底是什么时候开始反犹太的还有一些争论，但他不可能没有受到它的影响。

sentences.en: The thing is,
sentences.zh: 问题是，

sentences.en: his biographers don't think that it's pathological at that stage because he's just thinking about his rubbishy postcards and how miserable he is and Wagner and art and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他的传记作者认为在那个阶段这并不是病态的，因为他只是在想他的垃圾明信片，他有多痛苦，还有瓦格纳和艺术等等。

sentences.en: What clearly happens to him is he goes to the war because he's gone, he goes to Munich in the interim.
sentences.zh: 显然发生在他身上的是他去了战争，因为他去了，他在此期间去了慕尼黑。

sentences.en: There's the famous photo, isn't there, where he, in 1914, where he's, yeah, he's delighted like a lot of people are.
sentences.zh: 有一张著名的照片，不是吗，他在1914年，他，是的，他和很多人一样很高兴。

sentences.en: He really feels like, although he's born in Austria, he's from a German-speaking family, he's German-speaking himself, he feels like his destiny lies in a, in a,
sentences.zh: 他真的觉得，虽然他出生在奥地利，但他来自一个讲德语的家庭，他自己也讲德语，他觉得他的命运在于，在于，

sentences.en: in German-dom as he would no doubt have called it.
sentences.zh: 在德意志，正如他无疑会称呼的那样。

sentences.en: So he goes off to the war and I think what obviously happens, like to a lot of people in the war, and this isn't, again, not just in Germany, he's brutalized by it.
sentences.zh: 所以他去参加了战争，我想显然发生了什么，就像战争中的很多人一样，这不仅仅是在德国，他被战争摧残了。

sentences.en: He's surrounded by death.
sentences.zh: 他被死亡包围。

sentences.en: He's a dispatch runner.
sentences.zh: 他是一名传令兵。

sentences.en: I mean, lots of other dispatch runners are killed.
sentences.zh: 我是说，很多其他传令兵都被杀了。

sentences.en: It's not, you know, it's better than some posts in the army, but it's still not, it's not a barrel of laughs.
sentences.zh: 这并不是，你知道，这比军队里的一些岗位要好，但仍然不是，不是什么好玩的事。

sentences.en: So he's, he's inured to death and to suffering.
sentences.zh: 所以他，他习惯了死亡和痛苦。

sentences.en: I think this is the point that where, yeah, because before that nobody had said, oh, Hitler loves violence, he's an evil guy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是关键点，因为在那之前没有人说，哦，希特勒热爱暴力，他是个邪恶的人。

sentences.en: But I think at this point, you know, he's, he's surrounded by violence.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在这一点上，你知道，他，他被暴力包围了。

sentences.en: And then there's that sense of trauma and that stuff in Passavalk in the hospital has been invalided out.
sentences.zh: 然后就是那种创伤感，以及在帕塞瓦尔克的医院里发生的事情，他被伤退了。

sentences.en: I mean, you read in, in, so that, that thing that I read was, of course, from Mein Kampf, My Struggle, which he writes in the mid 1920s.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你读到的，所以，我读到的那东西，当然是来自《我的奋斗》，他在20世纪20年代中期写的。

sentences.en: And there's long passages in that, you know, it had all been in vain, in vain the sacrifices, in vain the hunger and thirSt.
sentences.zh: 里面有很长的段落，你知道的，这一切都白费了，牺牲白费了，饥饿和干渴也白费了。

sentences.en: Was it for this that the soldiers died in August and September 1914?
sentences.zh: 士兵们在1914年8月和9月牺牲，难道就是为了这个吗？

sentences.en: Had all this been done to enable a gang of despicable criminals to lay hands on the fatherland?
sentences.zh: 做这一切难道就是为了让一群卑劣的罪犯染指祖国吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, this is obsessive stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是走火入魔了。

sentences.en: So who, who is he referring to as the criminals?
sentences.zh: 那么，他所说的罪犯到底是指谁？

sentences.en: Is he referring to, well, they're called the November criminals, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他指的是那些所谓的“十一月罪犯”，对吧？

sentences.en: The, the, the democratic leaders who, um, agree to the armistice, or is he referring to the Jews already as the criminals?
sentences.zh: 是那些同意停战的民主派领导人，还是说他已经把犹太人称为罪犯了？

sentences.en: Both.
sentences.zh: 两者都有。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这样说很公允。

sentences.en: I think, um, he, I mean, don't forget he's writing those words later.
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯，他，我的意思是，别忘了这些话是他后来写的。

sentences.en: So he's looking back, but at the time there had been a rise.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在回顾，但在当时，确实出现了一股浪潮。

sentences.en: I mean, if Hitler was antisemitic already because of what he's experienced in Vienna, it makes sense that he's still antisemitic in 1918.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果希特勒因为在维也纳的经历已经变得反犹，那么他在1918年依然反犹也就说得通了。

sentences.en: There had been a rise in antisemitism in the last couple of years of the war as people look for scapegoats because of the shortages, the rationing.
sentences.zh: 战争最后几年反犹主义有所抬头，因为人们由于物资短缺和配给制度在寻找替罪羊。

sentences.en: And so there's a feeling that the Jews are profiteering.
sentences.zh: 于是就有一种感觉，认为犹太人在发国难财。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Speculators.
sentences.zh: 投机商。

sentences.en: People are wittering about Jewish spec, which is completely untrue and unfounded.
sentences.zh: 人们在喋喋不休地谈论犹太投机者，这完全是不实之词，毫无根据。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People are also saying, oh, the Jews aren't, Jewish Germans aren't doing their bit for the war effort.
sentences.zh: 人们还说，哦，犹太人没有，德国犹太人没有为战争尽力。

sentences.en: Again, completely unfounded.
sentences.zh: 同样，完全毫无根据。

sentences.en: Many, many.
sentences.zh: 非常多，非常多。

sentences.en: As evidenced by the cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 墓地就是证明。

sentences.en: By the cemeteries, by the fact that one of the guys who had nominated Hitler, the guy who nominated Hitler for the Iron Cross was a Jewish officer.
sentences.zh: 墓地就是证明，而且提名希特勒获得铁十字勋章的人中，就有一位是犹太军官。

sentences.en: But, you know, people lash out when they're angry and upset.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，人们在愤怒和心烦意乱时会口不择言。

sentences.en: And that's, this is what's happening, I think, across Germany.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这正是整个德国正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: But also, presumably, I mean, Hitler has an almost religious faith in Germandom, in the blood of the German people, in the blood of the Aryan people.
sentences.zh: 但大概也是因为，希特勒对德国精神、对德国人民的血统、对雅利安人的血统有着近乎宗教般的信仰。

sentences.en: And yet they have been defeated.
sentences.zh: 然而他们却战败了。

sentences.en: So therefore, the only way that he can explain that defeat is by treachery, whether it's democratic politicians or, more sinisterly,
sentences.zh: 因此，他解释战败的唯一方式就是归咎于背叛，无论是归咎于民主派政客，还是更阴险地，

sentences.en: this idea of a basilisk within the German bloodstream.
sentences.zh: 归咎于德国血脉中存在某种蛇怪的这种想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the nature of the defeat, Tom, explains that.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，战败的性质解释了这一点。

sentences.en: Because you see, Germans losing in 1918, they've gone on this tremendous offensive,
sentences.zh: 因为你看，德国人在1918年战败，他们发动了猛烈的攻势，

sentences.en: attempting to win the war in one blow before the Americans can really turn the balance of the war.
sentences.zh: 试图在美国真正扭转战争局势之前一举获胜。

sentences.en: And they've actually carried all before them, or appeared to in the sort of spring and summer of 1918.
sentences.zh: 在1918年的春夏，他们实际上势如破竹，或者看起来是这样。

sentences.en: And then they've, the great Ludendorff offensive runs out of steam, they've been driven back.
sentences.zh: 然后，伟大的鲁登道夫攻势后继乏力，他们被击退了。

sentences.en: And then suddenly it collapses very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 接着突然间，局势迅速崩溃。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of sense that the German people have not been prepared for the defeat.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，德国人民并没有为战败做好心理准备。

sentences.en: Crucially, of course, there are no Allied troops at that point on German soil.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，当时德国本土并没有盟军士兵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's all, it's an away fixture that they've lost, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一场他们输掉的客场比赛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To their surprise, because they thought they were winning.
sentences.zh: 他们感到很惊讶，因为他们以为自己正在获胜。

sentences.en: And actually, when the troops return to Berlin, Friedrich Ebert, who we'll talk about next time, who's a key figure in the creation of the Weimar Republic,
sentences.zh: 实际上，当军队回到柏林时，我们将要在下次讨论的弗里德里希·艾伯特——他是魏玛共和国建立的关键人物，

sentences.en: social democratic leader, he famously says to them, no enemy has defeated you.
sentences.zh: 社会民主党领袖，他曾对他们说过一句名言：没有敌人击败过你们。

sentences.en: And a lot of Germans believe that.
sentences.zh: 许多德国人都相信这一点。

sentences.en: They believe somehow they've lost the war, but they weren't really militarily defeated, which is completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们相信自己虽然输掉了战争，但在军事上并没有真正战败，这完全是错误的。

sentences.en: They were defeated on French and Belgian soil.
sentences.zh: 他们是在法国和比利时的土地上战败的。

sentences.en: But it's sort of been kept from them.
sentences.zh: 但这被隐瞒了起来。

sentences.en: And so they say, well, we've been stabbed in the back.
sentences.zh: 于是他们说，我们是被背后捅了一刀。

sentences.en: We've been betrayed by traitors and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们是被叛徒出卖了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Anyway, Hitler comes back to Munich, where he'd been before.
sentences.zh: 总之，希特勒回到了他之前待过的慕尼黑。

sentences.en: He comes back on the 21st of November, 1918.
sentences.zh: 他在1918年11月21日回来。

sentences.en: And at that point, Munich is already in utter, utter chaos.
sentences.zh: 那时，慕尼黑已经陷入了彻底的混乱。

sentences.en: So when the Kaiser's regime fell apart in the final days of the war, across Germany, people had just sort of randomly seized power in different places.
sentences.zh: 所以当德皇政权在战争最后几天瓦解时，德国各地的人们只是在不同地方随意地夺取了权力。

sentences.en: In Munich, power had been seized by a man who could have been designed to provoke Hitler.
sentences.zh: 在慕尼黑，权力被一个仿佛专门为了激怒希特勒而设计出来的人夺取了。

sentences.en: He's a guy called Kurt Eisner.
sentences.zh: 他叫库尔特·艾斯纳。

sentences.en: He's a theater critic.
sentences.zh: 他是一名戏剧评论家。

sentences.en: He's a very sort of bohemian sort of cafe habitué.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常波西米亚风格的咖啡馆常客。

sentences.en: He wears a black cloak and steel-rimmed glasses.
sentences.zh: 他穿着黑色斗篷，戴着钢框眼镜。

sentences.en: He's not even from Munich.
sentences.zh: 他甚至不是慕尼黑人。

sentences.en: He's from Berlin, and he's also Jewish, and he's very left-wing.
sentences.zh: 他来自柏林，而且是犹太人，还是极左翼。

sentences.en: So he basically sets up his own little Bavarian Republic in Munich.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上在慕尼黑建立了自己的小巴伐利亚共和国。

sentences.en: It's a complete shambles.
sentences.zh: 简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: Everybody on the right says, oh, my God, this Jewish theater critic has seized power.
sentences.zh: 右翼的所有人都说，天哪，这个犹太戏剧评论家夺取了权力。

sentences.en: What the hell's going on?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: He's assassinated.
sentences.zh: 他被暗杀了。

sentences.en: An even crazier regime comes in, the Bavarian Council Republic, under another – this time it's a poet and playwright called Ernst Toller.
sentences.zh: 一个更疯狂的政权上台了，即巴伐利亚苏维埃共和国，领导人是另一位——这次是一位名叫恩斯特·托勒的诗人和剧作家。

sentences.en: They're utterly ludicrous.
sentences.zh: 他们简直荒唐透顶。

sentences.en: Because that's the weird thing about this, is, of course, Hitler is an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 因为这正是奇怪的地方，当然，希特勒也是个艺术家。

sentences.en: You have all these guys who are kind of various playwrights and critics and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你有所有这些家伙，他们都是各种剧作家、评论家之类的。

sentences.en: It's basically people from the arts pages of newspapers all staging coups, trying to set up dictatorships.
sentences.zh: 基本上都是报纸艺术版的人在发动政变，试图建立独裁统治。

sentences.en: You know my view, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的观点，汤姆。

sentences.en: Artistic people should never be allowed anywhere near politics.
sentences.zh: 搞艺术的人永远不应该被允许靠近政治。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Ernst Toller's regime.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以恩斯特·托勒的政权。

sentences.en: So they declared war on Switzerland for not lending them 60 railway locomotives.
sentences.zh: 他们向瑞士宣战，因为瑞士没有借给他们60台火车头。

sentences.en: One of his ministers famously sends a telegram to Moscow asking for help because he says the previous minister has stolen the key to the ministerial toilet.
sentences.zh: 他的一位部长曾发了一封电报给莫斯科求援，因为他说上一任部长偷走了部长级厕所的钥匙。

sentences.en: So it's absolutely shambolic.
sentences.zh: 所以这简直是一场闹剧。

sentences.en: That regime is then toppled by communists, a much more hardline communist regime, which is very much in touch with what's going on in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 那个政权随后被共产党推翻了，一个更强硬的共产主义政权，与莫斯科的联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: They do think this would appeal to you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他们确实认为这会吸引你，汤姆。

sentences.en: One of their first initiatives is to turn a church in Munich into a temple of reason.
sentences.zh: 他们的首要举措之一是将慕尼黑的一座教堂变成理性神庙。

sentences.en: Yeah, very, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常，是的。

sentences.en: Very Robespierre-iSt.
sentences.zh: 非常有罗伯斯庇尔式的风格。

sentences.en: Very Robespierre-ist behavior, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实是非常罗伯斯庇尔式的行为。

sentences.en: So Munich is then retaken, and it's retaken by a group who a lot of people say anticipate the Nazis in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 所以慕尼黑随后被收复了，收复它的一群人被许多人认为在各方面都预示了纳粹的出现。

sentences.en: They're called the Freikorps, the Free Corps.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为“自由军团”。

sentences.en: And these are basically returning soldiers who, they've come back from the war.
sentences.zh: 这些人基本上是刚从战场回来的士兵。

sentences.en: Some of them, it's still in disbelief that they've lost at all.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人仍然不敢相信自己竟然战败了。

sentences.en: And these are the same guys who are putting down the communists in Berlin as well.
sentences.zh: 这些人也是在柏林镇压共产党人的同一批人。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。
